verdict.rationale: Orb documents several pieces that help ops change pricing safely: testing pricing changes against historical usage, per-subscription edits that leave the plan itself untouched, previewing invoice impact, and plan changes with proration and a preserved audit trail. There is no evidence of explicit plan versioning, a grandfathering mechanism, or bulk tooling to move cohorts of subscribers to new prices, and edits are documented only for a single subscription. Missing for 10: versioned plans, explicit grandfathering of existing subscribers, bulk or cohort migration tools, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an ops user, I can change pricing without breaking existing subscribers — versioned plans, grandfathering, and bulk migration tools for moving cohorts to new prices

citations.quote: Test pricing changes against historical usage before deploying.
Subscription Edits let you change a single subscription's pricing configuration directly from Orb's web interface or via the API
Preview the billing and invoice impact before you save, so you can confirm how charges and invoices will look.
When you change plans, the subscription ID remains the same, but Orb maintains a complete audit trail of every plan assignment.
